newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile halts Quinenco IPO, citing newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Chile halts Quinenco IPO, citing newspaper.

text.p: Chilean regulators ordered financial and industrial holding company Quinenco SA to halt its Initial Public Offering after the company published an ad announcing the offer before the shares were placed.

In a toughly worded statement, the Stocks and Securities Superintendency said Quinenco had, "compromised the public interest and the protection of investors" by buying the ad in the newspaper El Mercurio on Wednesday.
The superintendency ordered Quinenco to take out another ad in the same newspaper within 24 hours, announcing the cancellation of its IPO.

Quinenco -- the holding company for the Luksic group, one of Chile's most powerful business families -- had planned to place shares this month on both the Santiago Stock Exchange and foreign markets with American Depositary Receipts.
It was not immediately clear if the order halted only the local share placement, or the ADR placement as well.
The superintendency, Chile's equivalent of the U.S. Securities and Exchanges Commission, also ordered Quinenco to pay a fine of 400 Unidades de Fomento currency units ($13,000).

"The initial public offering by Quinenco SA is suspended, so long as the process of inscription of the shares has not been completed," said the statement, signed by superintendent Daniel Yarur and secretary-general Rodrigo Costa.
The problem with the ad in El Mercurio was that it indicated the placement date as between June 11 and June 24, said the statement.
"The company's shares in question are currently in the process of inscription by the Securities Registry, an inscription which, as of June 11, 1997, has not been completed," said the statement.
The suspension followed a series of news articles in El Mercurio this week about Quinenco's IPO and its planned ADR placement.
Quinenco would be the 21st Chilean company to place publicly-traded ADRs.
